title: feat(dialect): Add Grok CLI / xAI system prompt generator with tool schemas
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

xAI's Grok Bot and Grok CLI support agentic workflows and custom system routines. Currently, Cinch supports 10 harnesses but lacks a native adapter for Grok.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

xAI Grok documentation specifies system instruction formatting and function definitions adhering to standard OpenAPI/JSON schema function calling.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `src/cinch/dialects/grok.py`:
1. Compile Cinch skills to Grok routine format (`.grok/skills/<name>.md`).
2. Strip unsupported frontmatter and inject markdown instructions with function parameters.
3. Add unit tests and conformance fixtures in `tests/conformance/grok/`.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] `cinch sync --target grok` generates valid `.grok/skills/`.
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/test_translation.py` verify output formatting.
- [ ] Documentation updated in README harness matrix.

title: feat(mcp): Bidirectional MCP prompt exporter (expose Cinch skills as MCP prompts)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

MCP clients (like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Zed) support `prompts/list` and `prompts/get`. Exposing Cinch skills through an MCP prompt server allows any MCP-compatible client to invoke Cinch skills dynamically without manual installation.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Anthropic's Model Context Protocol Python SDK (`mcp.server.fastmcp`) allows defining prompts using decorators.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch mcp-server`:
1. Spin up a lightweight FastMCP STDIO server.
2. Expose all discovered skills in `.skills/` as MCP Prompts.
3. Support dynamic arguments via prompt templates.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Server responds to `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` via JSON-RPC.
- [ ] Fast startup (<50ms) using zero heavy dependencies.
- [ ] Integration test with mock MCP client.

title: feat(lsp): Implement lightweight Language Server Protocol (LSP) for skill frontmatter autocompletion
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

When writing skills in VS Code, Cursor, or Zed, authors lack autocompletion for frontmatter fields (`name`, `description`, `paths`, `compatibility`, `variables`), leading to typos and invalid configurations.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`yaml-language-server` and `ast-grep` provide real-time diagnostics, hover tooltips, and completion items using standard LSP JSON-RPC.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

Implement `cinch lsp`:
1. Single-file stdlib JSON-RPC LSP server.
2. Provides completions for schema fields and dialect names.
3. Emits hover documentation explaining harness-specific limitations.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Works with any LSP-compliant editor (VS Code, Zed, Neovim).
- [ ] Diagnostics flagged on unrecognized frontmatter keys.
- [ ] Unit tests covering LSP request/response cycle.

title: feat(policy): Corporate skill compliance & safety policy enforcement (`.cinchpolicy.yml`)
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Enterprise security teams require strict governance over AI prompts (e.g. banning `eval`, forbidding outbound network tool invocations, requiring approved license tags, enforcing maximum token budgets).

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

Open Policy Agent (OPA), `conftest`, and Semgrep enforce declarative security policies across repository assets.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

1. Support `.cinchpolicy.yml` defining validation rules.
2. Check skills during `cinch check` against the policy.
3. Fail CI with descriptive violation messages if a rule is breached.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Configurable policies for disallowed keywords, missing fields, and token limits.
- [ ] Clean CLI error reporting with exit code 1.
- [ ] Unit tests for policy evaluation.

title: feat(wasm): WebAssembly-compiled Cinch engine for interactive in-browser skill playground
body:
## Problem Statement / Background

Prospective users and team members want to try Cinch and see how their markdown skills translate across 10 dialects without installing Python or cloning a repository.

## Inspiration from State-of-the-Art Tools

`pyodide`, Ruff's WebAssembly playground, and SQL.js run Python and Rust tooling directly in browser clients with zero server backend.

## Proposed Solution & Architecture

1. Package Cinch core translation logic for Pyodide / WebAssembly.
2. Build a minimal static HTML/JS playground hosted on GitHub Pages.
3. Split-screen: Left is markdown editor, Right shows live tabs for all 10 compiled dialects.

## Acceptance Criteria & Test Plan

- [ ] Compiles skills in-browser in <10ms via Pyodide.
- [ ] Deployed to `00200200.github.io/cinch`.
- [ ] Automated end-to-end smoke test.
